newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM declines comment on Northwest rumours.
newsitem.headline: KLM declines comment on Northwest rumours.

text.p: Dutch carrier KLM on Tuesday declined to comment on reports it was close to clinching an agreement with U.S. partner Northwest on deepening their alliance in return for the sale of KLM's stake in Northwest.
"We are still in talks...when we have something to say on this issue we will do so," KLM spokesman Peter Wellhuener said.
Dutch daily De Telegraaf on Tuesday cited "management sources" as saying a deal on a longer-term partnership could be unveiled some time this week.
The airlines' dispute over KLM's Northwest stake has proved a stumbling block to stepping up their lucrative operational alliance.
Until now the partnership, under which the two airlines operate as one on transatlantic routes, has been based on short-term contracts.
Longer term deals would enable the pair to achieve even greater synergy benefits.
KLM confirmed earlier this month that selling its 19 percent Northwest stake was "an option" in resolving the dispute, which centres on Northwest's fears the Dutch airline is out to gain control.
Wellhuener said on Tuesday that a Northwest stake sale was still an option, but would not comment on the progress of talks.
On a depressed Amsterdam stock exchange, KLM shares added 0.30 guilders to 71.80 in early trade on Tuesday.
